content_html:
“Dream within a Dream” — A Nested View of Experience

Waking perception is a constrained simulation and sleep-dreaming is a deeper, less‑constrained simulation within it.

Outer layers constrain inner ones. As constraints relax (less sensory input, reduced executive control), experience becomes more dreamlike; as metacognition rises (lucidity), awareness can recognize the constructed nature of the layer it inhabits.

  • Descartes’ challenge: Dreams can mimic waking; sensory certainty is questionable.
  • Predictive processing: Waking is a controlled hallucination constrained by data; dreams are the same engine offline.
  • Contemplative traditions: Waking life is “dreamlike” (Buddhist śūnyatā/emptiness; Vedāntic māyā).
  • Lucidity & metacognition: Awareness can sometimes “wake up” within a layer and recognize its constructed nature.
